extracted.intended_audience: educational institution officials and administrators (e.g., Title IX Coordinators, school legal counsel, disability services staff), K-12 and postsecondary recipients subject to Title IX
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards implementing 34 CFR §106.40(b)(3) on reasonable modifications, leaves, and voluntary separate programs for students who are pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions; explains roles, interplay with other laws, privacy, and procedural obligations for recipients and Title IX Coordinators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable modifications because of pregnancy or related conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must make reasonable modifications to the recipient's policies, practices, or procedures as necessary to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access to the recipient's education program or activity for a student who is pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifications must be individualized to each student's pregnancy/related condition and needs; the student need not propose a particular modification; recipients may consider whether the student has a preferred modification, whether alternatives exist, and the feasibility of a modification. The Department provides examples (e.g., breaks from class for lactation or other health needs including eating, drinking, restroom use; access to online/homebound instruction — clarified that online need not be homebound). If more than one reasonable modification would address the student's needs, the recipient has discretion in what to offer. The recipient bears the burden of demonstrating that a particular modification would fundamentally alter the nature of its education program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individualized consideration of modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.40(b)(3)(ii) requires consideration on a basis individualized to each student's pregnancy or related condition and needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may evaluate factors such as the student's preferred modification, available alternatives, and feasibility. The list of examples in the regulation is non-exhaustive. Recipients have discretion when multiple reasonable options exist. Students are not limited by the recipient's past practices or the absence of precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient is ultimately responsible for implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient, not the Title IX Coordinator, is ultimately responsible for implementing requests for reasonable modifications and other specific actions under §106.40(b)(3)(ii)-(vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised text to clarify recipient responsibility while the Title IX Coordinator coordinates. Recipients may delegate implementation tasks to appropriate staff or departments but must ensure consistent compliance under Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator's role—to coordinate with oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator must coordinate actions under §106.40(b)(3)(i) through (vi) and retain ultimate oversight to ensure consistent compliance under Title IX and the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coordinator can serve as a point of contact, communicate approved modifications to students and staff, and coordinate multiple departments. The Coordinator may delegate duties but must retain oversight; the Department declined to further limit the Coordinator's coordinating role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation permitted with retention of oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient or Title IX Coordinator may delegate specific duties related to reasonable modifications to other personnel, provided the Title IX Coordinator retains ultimate oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation enables assignment to personnel best positioned to perform duties, address conflicts of interest, and align with administrative structures. Recipients may delegate to offices that support students with disabilities or other departments as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to document reasonable modifications by Title IX Coordinator
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department removed the proposed requirement that the Title IX Coordinator 'document' reasonable modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are not required by §106.40(b)(3)(ii) to maintain documentation of compliance with reasonable modifications, though they may voluntarily keep records. Any personally identifiable information in such records would be subject to §106.44(j) restrictions on disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: No mandatory consultation with disability services in every case
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require a Title IX Coordinator to consult with disabilities support staff or a student's IEP/Section 504 team in every instance of providing reasonable modifications for pregnancy or related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether consultation is required is fact-specific. Some cases (e.g., mobility-impacting disability combined with pregnancy) may require IEP/504 coordination; other cases may not. Mandatory consultation could infringe student privacy when the student does not want to disclose pregnancy-related information beyond the Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy protections and limits on information gathering
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have no education-related need to ask how or where a student will obtain abortion-related care; unnecessary or invasive questions could constitute sex discrimination and chill students from seeking modifications or leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asking for sensitive details (e.g., circumstances of pregnancy, marital status) may be impermissible, particularly if informed by sex stereotypes. Recipients should treat information similarly to other temporary medical conditions and avoid different treatment in the abortion context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of pregnancy covered as a pregnancy-related condition
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'pregnancy or related conditions' includes pregnancy, childbirth, termination of pregnancy, lactation, related medical conditions, and recovery periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable modifications under §106.40(b)(3)(ii) and voluntary leaves under §106.40(b)(3)(iv) apply to termination of pregnancy. Such modifications or leave are not considered 'benefits or services' under 20 U.S.C. 1688 and do not require a recipient to fund or perform abortions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary leave of absence for pregnancy or related conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.40(b)(3)(iv), a recipient must allow a student who is pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions to voluntarily take a leave of absence for at least the time medically necessary as determined by the student's licensed healthcare provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A voluntary leave is distinct from a modification and ensures students can take medically necessary time without being denied access; leave is not a 'benefit or service' related to abortion per 20 U.S.C. 1688.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction from ADA/Section 504 obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A pregnancy-related condition need not qualify as a disability under the ADA to qualify for reasonable modifications under Title IX; obligations under §106.40(b)(3)(ii) are distinct from ADA/Section 504 obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The framework for pregnancy-related reasonable modifications is similar to Title II of the ADA and may invite collaboration, but compliance with Title IX does not supplant or expand ADA/Section 504 rules. Recipients must still comply with all applicable civil rights laws separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to student-employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The obligation to provide reasonable modifications under §106.40(b)(3)(ii) applies to a 'student' (as defined in §106.2) regardless of whether that individual is also an employee of the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an employee is enrolled in the recipient's education program, the recipient must offer modifications sufficient to allow the employee to continue educational progress. Grievance procedures under §106.45 (and if applicable §106.46) apply to complaints alleging failure to take actions under §106.40(b)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures apply to failures under §106.40(b)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with grievance procedures outlined in §106.45 and, if applicable, §106.46 for complaints alleging a recipient failed to take specific actions required under §106.40(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.46(b) discusses application of grievance procedures to sex-based harassment complaints (which may include pregnancy harassment) involving postsecondary student-employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to extend modifications to applicants denied
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require that §106.40(b)(3)(ii) be applied to applicants for admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion refers to §106.21(c)(1) for more detail; recipients are not required by these final regulations to provide reasonable modifications to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology: use of 'reasonable modifications' rather than 'accommodations'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department retained the term 'reasonable modifications' (rather than 'reasonable accommodations') for §106.40(b)(3)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term is appropriate and straightforward; under the final regulations a recipient may implement a modification only for one student or implement a broader change affecting many students. The regulatory framework draws primarily from Title II of the ADA (28 CFR 35.130(b)(7)), which uses 'reasonable modifications.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost and burden considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifications unrelated to lactation and leave generally involve modest changes (e.g., larger desk, more frequent bathroom breaks, temporary elevator access); the Department finds costs or burdens do not outweigh benefits of clarifying recipient obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to extend modifications beyond students who are pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions. Policies related to parental/family status cannot treat students differently based on sex (e.g., permitting leave for only one sex based on 'natural caregiver' stereotypes would violate Title IX). The Regulatory Impact Analysis contains a more detailed discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary and comparable separate programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in any separate program based on pregnancy or related conditions must be voluntary and such programs must be comparable to those offered to students who are not pregnant or parenting (final §106.40(b)(1) and (3)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must not coerce or pressure students into alternative programs. Comments requesting 'substantially equal' or more specific tests were declined; the Department notes longstanding regulation requiring that admittance be 'completely voluntary.' Examples indicate coercion has occurred when counselors pressure pregnant students into lower-quality alternative programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on coercion into separate programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must not force, require, or pressure a student who is pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions to participate in a separate portion of the education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The use of 'voluntarily' in the regulation means recipients must not coerce or pressure any student to participate. OCR guidance (1991, 2013 Pregnancy Pamphlet) reiterates that the regulations prohibit requiring or pressuring students into separate programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may adopt additional coordination mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the final regulations prevents a recipient from adopting additional mechanisms to coordinate compliance with relevant laws to maximize protection from discrimination and minimize redundancy or burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may implement extra steps to coordinate Title IX compliance with other institutional processes, provided they respect privacy and statutory limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student is not required to propose specific modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not incumbent on the student to propose or suggest any particular reasonable modification in order for the recipient to offer reasonable modifications with the student's input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must consider reasonable options and may offer modifications even if the student does not identify a specific needed accommodation; the process is collaborative and individualized.
